story.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats

draft:
When a language model spots a new enzyme, the lab bench gets a fresh partner.  

Claude, Anthropic’s LLM, flagged a previously unknown enzyme system that carries CRISPR‑like repeat sequences. The pattern suggests a natural, programmable nuclease—something we’ve only seen in a handful of bacterial families.  

- This is the first time an AI has moved from text prediction to proposing a concrete biochemical mechanism. It shows that large models can sift through massive sequence databases and literature faster than any human team, surfacing hypotheses that would otherwise stay buried.  
- The discovery also forces us to rethink validation pipelines. If an AI can generate a candidate, the bottleneck shifts to rapid experimental confirmation and clear attribution of intellectual property.  

If the system proves functional, we could add a whole new class of gene‑editing tools to the CRISPR toolbox, lowering barriers for labs that lack deep bio‑engineering resources.  

What other scientific fields could be accelerated by AI‑driven hypothesis mining?
